blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 84 in June to 94 in October (+11.9%), and it took 8.2% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 40 in June to 34 in October (−15.0%), and it took 2.6% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Bear Creek Green Timbers for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in August, October (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Bear Creek Green Timbers
What trades here

items.t: No typical lot size, lot count or lot price is stated.
A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is not fee-simple.
Named buildings/complexes — cross-reference only, never land: None is a land development, a subdivision or a lot offering here.

The one documented change at the sub-area's edge is transit infrastructure — Green Timbers Station on the Surrey Langley SkyTrain (anticipated in-service 2029) — which is a project station, not a development site and not land inventory.
A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)

Municipal geography: the ground sits inside the City of Surrey. The City places Bear Creek Park in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre, while Green Timbers is the urban-forest ground in the city's north-centre; the City lists seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey, Whalley) and "Bear Creek Green Timbers" is not one of them.

The two green spaces the name joins: Bear Creek Park (placed by the City in Whalley) and Green Timbers Urban Forest, whose westernmost edge will host the Green Timbers SkyTrain Station at 140 Street and Fraser Highway.
The board does not publish sub-area medians.

Transit edge: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029; Green Timbers Station (140 Street and Fraser Highway) is its station at this sub-area's north edge.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: SSMUH / added units (Surrey framework, adopted Jul 8, 2024): a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, on eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² within the Urban Containment Boundary. Added-unit permission is not permission to subdivide and does not create new lots.

Coach houses and garden suites: all Surrey residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes also allow a coach house or garden suite; the unit must be at least 35 m² and at most 75 m², rising to 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the existing house or duplex is below maximum FAR; smaller R3–R6 lots require lane access for a coach house; one extra parking space is required.

Streamside / riparian — the creek diligence item for this sub-area: Surrey's streamside setbacks are defined in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, with different setbacks applied to various types of streams, complemented by the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit (SEDP) process — a parcel near Bear Creek or another watercourse is checked against its stream class in COSMOS and Part 7A, and no single setback figure is stated for the sub-area because the bylaw sets them by class.

ALR block: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: The board name and the City's map disagree, and both are right. "Bear Creek Green Timbers" exists only as a board sub-area; the City frames the same area through Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford, and places Bear Creek Park itself in Whalley beside the Surrey Arts Centre. A City plan search run under the board name finds nothing — search by parcel in COSMOS instead.

One name, two forms on the same avenue. The Trails name on 84 Avenue covers a townhouse component and an apartment building at different addresses (plus a directory address that could not be resolved to either in the townhomes pass) — a name-based search mixes them, and neither is land.
The "164-acre Bear Creek Park" figure is listing text, not a City figure.
Small counts make this sub-area's pace a signal, not a trend.
Suite income is the detached story here — and the permit is the diligence.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: streets and boundaries

items.t: Bear Creek Green Timbers is one Fraser Valley board sub-area with a compound name — not two separate neighbourhoods — joining the Bear Creek Park ground in the west with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground in the east. (SnapStats, September 2026)

The City does not use the name as a community: the City lists seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey, Whalley) and places Bear Creek Park in Whalley, so this board sub-area lies over ground the City frames through Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford.
The two name-giving green spaces face each other across the sub-area: Bear Creek Park at 13750 88 Avenue in the west, and Green Timbers Urban Forest at the 14600 block of 100 Avenue in the east.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is detached-led: established houses on larger, tree-covered lots around the two parks, with a condo cluster on 81a Avenue and townhouse complexes toward the Fleetwood and Guildford edges.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Green Timbers is a protected urban forest by public vote: Surrey residents voted in 1988 and again in 1996 to designate part of the park as an urban forest, a protected natural legacy — lots at its edge sit beside land the City holds as protected, not as a future subdivision.

Bear Creek is a fish-bearing creek: the City's park page notes spawning salmon or trout visible from the trail, so lots backing onto the creek corridor can carry riparian setback and tree rules — check the parcel in the City's COSMOS map.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Green Timbers Urban Forest holds over 10 kilometres of nature trails, a regularly stocked fishing lake (fishing from shore only — no watercraft, wading or swimming), picnic areas and the Surrey Nature Centre, all in second-growth forest.

The forest is called British Columbia's "Birthplace of Reforestation": the land was completely logged by 1929, then replanted and run as a forestry school and nursery before becoming a park in 1974, and a glacial erratic — a boulder carried by glacial ice — sits in its northwestern trails.
Bear Creek Park's walking track is a 365-metre, 4-lane rubberized track at the 88 Avenue entrance, lit for evening walkers and open year-round.
The Surrey Arts Centre shares Bear Creek Park's address, 13750 88 Avenue — the park is also the city's arts venue, with the Bear Creek Stadium athletics facility on the same area.

Bear Creek Park is at capacity for large-scale community events: the City states no community event applications are being accepted for the park at this time, and certain track and field amenities are being upgraded, closed until spring 2026.
The park's spray park was rebuilt in 2026 in four colour-coded sensory zones, designed with the Surrey Accessibility Leadership Team — a new facility fact for families on the surrounding streets.

A heritage marker in Bear Creek Park shows a historic map of local landowners, self-titled "stump farmers," from around 1940, and acknowledges the forced removal of Japanese Canadians during the Second World War.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: development and new projects

items.t: Green Timbers Station, Surrey Langley SkyTrain (Province of BC / TransLink) — station at 140 Street and Fraser Highway on the westernmost edge of Green Timbers Urban Forest, serving the Jim Pattison Outpatient Care and Surgery Centre, the BC RCMP E-Divisional Headquarters and Surrey Memorial Hospital; status: project in delivery, anticipated in-service date 2029 (as of November 3, 2026).

Bear Creek Park Stadium and track upgrades (City of Surrey) — throwing fields being upgraded to international sport standards and electrical capacity being increased for festivals; certain track and field amenities closed until spring 2026, and the spray park was rebuilt in 2026; status: ongoing improvements per the City park page (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: getting around

items.t: Route 325 runs between Surrey Central Station and Newton Exchange via 72 Ave, 140 St and 102 Ave, crossing the Green Timbers side of the sub-area on 140 Street.

The nearest SkyTrain today is King George Station; measured from Bear Creek Park (13750 88 Avenue) in the What's Nearby pass, it is a 3.9-minute drive (2.84 km) and Surrey Central Station a 5.7-minute drive (3.76 km), OSRM routing measured 2026-11-02.
From 2029 (anticipated), Green Timbers Station at 140 Street and Fraser Highway puts the sub-area's east side on the Expo Line — the first rail service inside the sub-area.

blocks.text: Bear Creek Green Timbers: risks and due diligence

items.t: Bear Creek's salmon and trout spawning makes its corridor a riparian check: any lot backing onto the creek should be tested for riparian setbacks and tree-protection rules in COSMOS before a buyer prices a coach house or an addition.

Green Timbers Lake is for wildlife and fishing only — no watercraft, wading or swimming, and dogs must stay on leash and out of the water — which sets what "lakefront" recreation actually means on the forest's edge streets.

Station construction is the near-term disruption: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain is being built along Fraser Highway at the sub-area's east edge with an anticipated 2029 opening, so Fraser Highway-fronting lots carry construction and guideway effects the park pages do not describe — check the project site for the current works map.

faq.a: One board sub-area with a compound name — a single sub-area of the Surrey community in the SnapStats data, joining the Bear Creek Park ground (which the City places in Whalley) with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground. It is not one of the City's seven community names.
faq.q: Is Bear Creek Green Timbers one area or two?

faq.a: What trades as land is the existing fabric — detached house lots, including suite-heavy houses and the occasional lot marketed to builders in listing text — each checked parcel by parcel in COSMOS.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot here?

faq.a: The streamside check: Surrey's setbacks sit in Part 7A of Bylaw No. 12000 and vary by stream class, with the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit process alongside — read the parcel's class and permit-area position in COSMOS before design work. No single setback figure is stated for the sub-area, because the bylaw does not set one.
faq.q: What creek or park diligence applies to a lot near Bear Creek Park?

faq.a: One secondary suite per dwelling unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area and never inside a coach house or garden suite; a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR, with lane access required on smaller lots and one extra parking space). Verify a suite's permit status rather than relying on listing text.
faq.q: Can a house lot here add a suite or a coach house?

faq.a: Different permissions: SSMUH allows 3–4 units on most lots by size band (up to 6 near a frequent bus stop), but that does not create new lots; subdivision must meet the zone minimum in Bylaw No. 12000 and the servicing requirements under the Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830, confirmed with the City per parcel.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a lot here, or build multiple units instead?

faq.a: Neither is duplex stock. Read the address and the MLS sub-type, not just the name.
faq.q: A listing says "Kings Landing" or "The Trails" — is it a duplex?

faq.a: Only if that half is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot.
faq.q: A card shows a half duplex here — can I buy just that half?

faq.a: One secondary suite per dwelling unit (at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never inside a coach house or garden suite), a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR, lane access required for a coach house on smaller lots, one extra parking space), and 3–4 SSMUH units on most lots by size band, up to 6 near a frequent bus stop. A suite built without permits is not retroactively legalized by the SSMUH changes — verify a suite's permit status rather than relying on listing text.
faq.q: Can I add a suite or a coach house to a house here?

faq.a: One board sub-area with a compound name. Board data carries a single "Bear Creek Green Timbers" sub-area of Surrey, joining the Bear Creek Park ground — which the City places in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre — with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground to the east. Buyers say the two park names separately, but listings and statistics use the single combined label.
faq.q: Is Bear Creek Green Timbers one neighbourhood or two?

faq.a: TransLink states an anticipated in-service date of 2029 for the 16-kilometre Expo Line extension from King George Station to Langley City. Until then the station is a plan fact, not a service.
faq.q: When does SkyTrain reach Green Timbers?

faq.a: A health and public-safety cluster on Green Timbers Way. The SkyTrain project states Green Timbers Station will facilitate access to the Jim Pattison Outpatient Care and Surgery Centre, the BC RCMP E-Divisional Headquarters and Surrey Memorial Hospital — the institutions that share the forest's western edge along Fraser Highway.
faq.q: What is at Green Timbers besides the forest?

faq.a: Schools confirmed by address in and around this area include Bear Creek Elementary (13780 80 Ave), Green Timbers Elementary (8824 144 St), Frank Hurt Secondary (13940 77 Ave) and Enver Creek Secondary (14505 84 Ave), all School District 36. Catchments are address-based and which schools fall inside the board sub-area line is not published, so run the exact address in the district locator.
